## "Eigenvalue spectrum" in this corpus

The phrase is used in its **random-matrix-theory (RMT) sense** — the set of eigenvalues of a covariance/correlation matrix and how they distribute — and the corpus contains a tight cluster of papers built on exactly this idea. Here is the complete picture, cited by document and page.

### The core definition (the anchor document)
**"Recovering Structural Organization in Noisy Correlation Networks Using Financial Systems as a Testbed"** (`2607.10297`) gives the textbook definition. For an N×T panel of i.i.d. Gaussian returns, the eigenvalues λ of the random correlation matrix follow the **Marčenko–Pastur (MP) distribution**, and the **eigenvalue spectrum is bounded** by (p. 5):

- λ± = (1 ± √(1/Q))², with Q = T/N

Eigenvalues lying **above λ₊** carry genuine (non-random) structure; those inside [λ₋, λ₊] are noise. The paper decomposes the correlation matrix into a "structured mode" (the k eigenvalues above λ₊) and a "random mode" (the rest) (p. 5). Its Table 1 (p. 11) reports the measured spectra:

| Dataset | λ₋ | λ₊ | λ_max | % above λ₊ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| NIFTY 200 | 0.626 | 1.461 | 35.87 | 7.14% |
| NIFTY 500 | 0.473 | 1.722 | 68.62 | 3.85% |
| S&P 500 | 0.409 | 1.851 | 172.15 | 3.76% |

The single dominant λ_max (e.g. 172 vs. an MP edge of 1.85 for the S&P 500) is the familiar "market mode." Eigenmode plots against the MP bounds are in Figure 2 (p. 10).

### How neighboring papers use the same spectrum
- **"Iterative detection of global factors near the BBP phase transition"** (`2607.06908`) works directly with the ordered spectrum λ̃₁ ≥ … ≥ λ̃_p (p. 13).
